messages:
mika: Quick note - p99 for our small LLM inference path jumped ~55ms after last week's spot-cap bump in eu-central. Appears correlated with node churn and some AZ-level preemptions.

ben: Any quick metrics on per-AZ spot preempt rates? Could be a single noisy AZ.

mika: yes - eu-central-1b had a 3x elevation in spot evicts in the last 6h. Overall spot ratio for gpu-pool is 68%.

drew: Two immediate levers we can use: 1) make latency-sensitive pods prefer nodes labeled capacity-type=on-demand (nodeSelector/affinity), 2) gate autoscaler from picking exclusively spot nodes for these pods via a scheduler-extender.

sophia: We're already using priorityClass for interactive requests; combining that with scheduler-extender that scores nodes by capacity-type and projected preempt-risk could be better than taints alone.

mika: Agreed. Idea: implement a scheduler-extender that adds a risk score per node based on recent preemptions and AZ spot saturation. Score low -> prefer. Then weight that together with default binpacking.

ops-bot: note: cluster-autoscaler v1.25.3 scheduled for upgrade tonight (non-prod first).

julia: For node provisioning: can we add a "capacityProfile" label on nodepools (e.g., capacityProfile=spot,capacityProfile=on-demand,warmspare) and expose that to the extender? It makes policies simpler.

drew: yes. Proposed policy sketch: latency-critical pods labeled redwood/latency=high must have nodeAffinity -> capacityProfile=on-demand OR score nodes with capacityProfile=warmspare higher than spot. Extender enforces a minimum on-demand capacity fraction per AZ (configurable, default 40%).

sophia: Also consider using a preemptible handshake: on spot termination notice, our termination-handler annotates node with node.k8s.io/preempting=true and triggers an Extender API call to re-score that node as worst. Then the controller drains (graceful) with a 90s soft window for RPC pods, and checkpoint-migration for long jobs.

ben: Any thoughts on checkpoint flow? Last time we lost runs because eps weren't checkpointing fast enough.

mika: New proposal: pod-annotation `redwood/eviction-strategy: migrate|terminate|checkpoint`. The eviction-controller will:
- migrate: attempt to recreate a matching pod on warmspare/on-demand via a small rollout controller
- checkpoint: call sidecar endpoint /checkpoint, wait up to 3m, upload to s3, then terminate
- terminate: immediate graceful drain (default for batch).

drew: Example pod annotation snippet we can try in staging:
```yaml\nmetadata:\n  annotations:\n    redwood/eviction-strategy: migrate\nspec:\n  affinity:\n    nodeAffinity:\n      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:\n        nodeSelectorTerms:\n        - matchExpressions:\n          - key: capacityProfile\n            operator: In\n            values:\n            - on-demand
```

sophia: For autoscaler config, we should avoid aggressive downscale of warmspare nodes but allow scale-up fast. Suggested tuning: scaleDownUnneededTime: 20m, scaleDownUtilizationThreshold: 0.5, and use separate node-group for warmspare with min replicas=2 per AZ.

julia: Also add an AZ-level cap for spot share. Proposed default: max_spot_pct_per_az=60. When an AZ exceeds that, the provisioner will prefer on-demand or another AZ for scheduling. This avoids all-in-one-AZ spot saturation.

mika: Action items:
- drew: prototype scheduler-extender scoring (ETA 2d)
- julia: nodepool labeling + warmspare min-replicas per AZ (ETA EOD)
- sophia: eviction-strategy annotation spec + sidecar API contract (ETA 3d)
- ben: run AZ-saturation cost sim for max_spot_pct values 50/60/70 and share numbers (ETA 48h)

ops-bot: reminder: please file infra RFC for scheduler-extender before you start prototyping.

drew: will open RFC today and drop a PoC branch in infra repo. I'll canary in eu-west then us-west.

mika: Great. If the extender looks heavy, fallback plan is to add a lightweight webhook that injects preferredNode labels at pod admission time for our latency classes.

ben: +1. Also let's add a Slack alert when AZ spot-utilization > 65% so SRE can triage before user impact.

mika: Thanks all. We'll reconvene after the staging canary. :thumbsup:
